features.intro: Connect it, clean it, set it to repeat. That's most of it.

items.title: Plain English cleaning
items.body: Type something like "make every date YYYY-MM-DD" or "treat Acme Inc and ACME as one customer". It writes the step and shows you the result before anything changes.

items.title: A list of what's wrong
items.body: Each column is scanned for blanks, duplicates, odd values and mixed formats. You see the full list first, then decide.

items.title: Works with what you already use
items.body: CSV files, Google Sheets, MySQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, MongoDB, AWS, Databricks, Google Analytics 4 and more.

items.title: Steps you can reuse
items.body: Save a cleanup once and run it on every new file. Put it on a schedule if you'd rather not think about it.

items.title: SQL you can see and edit
items.body: Every step has SQL behind it. Copy it, change it, or write your own in the built-in editor.

items.title: Alerts before reports break
items.body: Get an email when a column changes shape or the numbers start to look off.

items.title: Private databases, handled
items.body: Reach a database behind a firewall through a secure tunnel. You don't open any ports.

items.title: Teams and approvals
items.body: Admin, Data Steward, Editor and Viewer roles. Sensitive sources can sit behind an approval step.

items.title: Add your data
items.body: Upload a CSV, paste a Google Sheet link, or connect a database.

items.title: Check what it found
items.body: Every problem is listed by column. Accept the fixes you like and describe the rest in your own words.

items.title: Download or repeat
items.body: Grab the clean file, send it to a destination, or save the steps to run again later.

alerts.body: Schedule a run and get an email if a column disappears, a type flips or the values drift. You hear about it before your client does.

items.q: What does The God's Tool do?
items.a: It cleans messy data. You upload a CSV or connect a Google Sheet or database, it lists the problems it finds, and you approve the fixes or describe your own in plain English. The steps can be saved and run again.

items.q: Can I clean a CSV or Google Sheet for free?
items.a: Yes. The free plan handles CSV files up to 5 MB and 5,000 rows per run, with up to 3 sources and 1 pipeline. New accounts also get 14 days with everything unlocked.

items.q: Do I need to know SQL or code?
items.a: No. You can do all of it by clicking and typing in plain English. If you do know SQL, every step shows the query behind it and you can edit it.

items.q: What are credits, and who are they for?
items.a: One credit covers one AI action, like asking it to write a cleaning step. They're useful if you only clean data now and then, because there is no monthly fee. They cost about $0.03 each, with a $2 minimum top-up.

items.q: Can I use it for client work?
items.a: Yes, plenty of freelancers do. The files are processed under your account, so check that your agreement with the client allows sharing their data with a tool like this.
Data is encrypted in transit and we don't share it with third parties. Google sign-in is only used to log you in, and a Google Sheet is read only when you connect it yourself.

items.q: Which data sources can I connect?
items.a: CSV, Google Sheets, MySQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, MongoDB, AWS RDS, S3, DynamoDB and Redshift, Google Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Databricks, REST APIs and Google Analytics 4.

items.q: What happens when the trial ends?
items.a: Your account moves to the free plan with its limits. Nothing is deleted, and you can upgrade or buy credits whenever you like.
Fill in the short form on this page. We read it and reply by email with a price for credits, seats or sources. There's no obligation to buy.
